objective: Find one bounded private-knowledge use case where the current Local Knowledge Terminal can genuinely help, then invite a fit-first pilot inquiry without implying an off-the-shelf product.

limits: Do not call the hardware ready to ship or imply that a standard kit is available.
Do not quote a price, delivery date, support term, license, corpus entitlement, model benchmark, or hardware specification that is not on current first-party evidence.
The public repository has no detected software license; describe it as public code, not open source, until the owner selects a license.
Ask about the collection, languages, intended readers, privacy needs, and existing hardware before discussing scope.
A useful technical answer must stand on its own before mentioning the pilot page.

funnel.free_value: Inspect the public code, tests, architecture, and durable product brief.
funnel.qualified_interest: Visit the pilot page or send a bounded use-case inquiry.
funnel.commercial_action: Agree on a reviewed scope and price only after the current software is shown to fit the collection and hardware.
funnel.gross_revenue_milestone: Record revenue only after confirmed payment; page visits and inquiries are not sales.

reddit.policy: Reply only to a current private/local knowledge-base problem after checking community rules. Solve the technical question first and disclose affiliation if the pilot page materially helps.

x.policy: A future first-party product post may show the real word-card or word-origin interface and ask for one bounded pilot use case. It must remain unscheduled until exact review.

instagram.policy: Use only the real current interface images. Describe the working software and pilot boundary; do not present a hardware mockup as inventory.

hackernews.policy: Hacker News prohibits generated or AI-edited comments. Discover needs only; do not create or send agent-authored replies.
